ORDER
IA-274 of 2026
(For leave to file appeal)
1. The Applicants/Appellants are, by way of this application, seeking
leave to file appeal against the order dated 10th November, 2025 passed
by the 1st Respondent – Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission
(hereinafter referred to as “the Commission”) in petition No. 2491 of 2025
filed by 3rd Respondent. It would be relevant to note here that the
Appellants were not a party to the said petition before the Commission but
are claiming to be “parties aggrieved” by the said impugned order of the
Commission and accordingly have sought permission to challenge the
said order of the Commission in this appeal.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 2 of 19

2. The Appellant No. 1 – Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Ltd. (in short
GUVNL) is a company incorporated under the provisions of the
Companies Act, 1956 and undertakes the functions of bulk purchase of
Electricity from the generators as well as other sources and bulk supply of
electricity to the distribution licensees in the State of Gujarat. The
Appellant Nos. 2 to 5 are the Distribution Licensees within the State of
Gujarat.
3. The 2nd Respondent – M/s Torrent Power Limited is also a
Distribution Licensees in the State of Gujarat operating in the areas of
Surat and Ahmedabad.
4. The 3rd Respondent- Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation
Limited (in short “GETCO”) is a transmission licensee as well as State
Transmission Utility (STU) in the State of Gujarat. The State Load
Despatch Centre (in short “SLDC”) is a separate devision of GETCO
discharging independent functions enumerated in the Electricity Act, 2003.
5. It appears that the Respondent No. 3 – GETCO had filed a petition
bearing No. 2419 of 2024 for true up for Financial Year 2023-24 and
determination of ARR as well as tariff for Financial Year 2025-26 to
Financial Year 2029-30. The 2nd Respondent had filed its objections to the
said petition on the issue of levy of Short Term Open Access (STOA)
charges. Upon following usual course in the said tariff petition which
included conducting public hearing, the petition was disposed of by the
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 3 of 19

Commission vide order dated 29th March, 2025. With regards to the issue
No. 10 formulated in the said petition relating to determination of
transmission charges, against which objections had been filed by 2nd
Respondent, the Commission observed that the matter is important and
needs to be examined in depth. Accordingly, it suggested 2nd Respondent
to file separate petition on this aspect.
6. In terms of the suggestion made by the Commission in the above
noted tariff order dated 29th March, 2025, the 2nd Respondent filed petition
bearing No.2491 of 2025 before the Commission seeking direction to 3rd
Respondent – GETCO to;
(a) Refund past period STOA charges as recovered from it for
the period Financial Year 2017-18 to Financial Year 2024-25
and;
(b) Treat all the Distribution Licensees including 2nd Respondent
uniformally for recovery of STOA charges for future period.
7. This petition has been allowed by the Commission vide order dated
10th November, 2025 thereby directing as under :-
“(a) GETCO shall adhere to Open Access mechanism for
grant of Short Term Open access and levy of STOA
charges without any discrimination in line with the
provisions of GERC Open Access Regulations.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 4 of 19

(b) GETCO/SLDC is directed to implement the decision in
Para No (a) above and file compliance affidavit within 2
months from the date of this Order.
(c) GETCO/SLDC shall verify the claims of the Petitioners
and refund the STOA Charges recovered from TPL –
Ahmedabad and Surat for Inter-State Short Term Bilateral
and Power Exchange Open Access Transactions w.e.f.
01.04.2017 till the date of this Order to pass on to TPL
Ahmedabad and Surat consumers.”
8. The Appellants seek to institute the instant appeal against the said
order dated 10th November, 2025.
9. The grounds upon which the Appellants are seeking leave to file
appeal against the said order dated 10th November, 2025 of the
Commission have been stated in paragraph No. 5 of application which is
extracted hereinbelow :-
“5. In view of the above, Applicants have also filed an Appeal
before the Hon'ble APTEL. (DFR No. 70 of 2026). It is the
submission of the Applicants that the State Commission has
ordered refund of STOA transmission charges to Torrent Power
on the alleged ground that such charges were not being levied
on Applicants, in complete ignorance of the fact that Applicants
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 5 of 19

are the bulk procurer of power in the State and the holding
company of the State Distribution Licensees, who bear the
transmission charges of GETCO on a residual basis. Any refund
of STOA charges to Torrent Power results in a corresponding
increase in the transmission burden on Applicants, thereby
causing financial prejudice to them. Further, the State
Commission has recorded findings on the GUVNL's
Transmission Service Agreement, nature of open access and
alleged differential treatment, without impleading them, making
it a necessary and affected party. Applicants are therefore
seeking the leave to file the present appeal.”
10. We have heard Mr. Anand K. Ganesan, Learned Counsel for the
Appellants/Applicants and Ms. Deepa Chawan, Learned Senior Counsel
appearing on behalf of 2nd Respondent. We have also perused written
submissions filed by the Learned Counsels.
11. Here it would be pertinent to note that Ms. Mandakini Ghosh, Learned
Counsel for 3rd Respondent – GETCO submitted that she does not oppose
the instant application.
12. Learned Counsel for the Appellants/applicants strenuously argued
that Appellants were necessary party to the petition before the Commission
in which the impugned order has been passed but were not made parties
to the same despite specific objections having been raised by the 3rd
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 6 of 19

Respondent – GETCO. He would submit that since Appellant No. 1 is the
bulk procurer of power in the State of Gujarat on behalf of Appellant Nos. 2
to 5 which are Distribution Licensees in the State, the Appellants bear the
aggregate revenue requirement of GETCO on a residual basis and any
recovery from the other open access consumers reduced the burden of the
Appellants. It is submitted that consequently, any reduction in the charges
qua open access consumers increases the burden on the Appellants. Her
submission is that any refund of STOA charges to 2nd Respondent and
future non-payment of such charges by 2nd Respondent would result in
corresponding increase in the financial burden on the Appellants thereby
causing financial prejudice to them. She would further argue that the
Commission, in the impugned order, has discussed the terms of
Transmission Service Agreement (TSA) dated 1st April, 2005 to which the
Appellants are signatories which could not have been done without
impleading the Appellants as parties.
13. According to the Learned Counsel, the Appellants are “aggrieved
persons” within ambit of the said term used in Section 111 of the Electricity
Act, 2003 and thus, are entitled to file the instant appeal challenging the
above noted order dated 10th November, 2025. She would place a reliance
upon the judgement of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Municipal Corporation
for Greater Bombay vs. Lala Pancham and Ors. (1965) 1 SCR 542:AIR
1965 SC 1008 and judgement of this Tribunal in Emmar MGF Construction
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 7 of 19

Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission in Appeal No. 123 of
2008 decided on 8th September, 2009 to canvass that the phrase “Person
Aggrieved” must be given widest amplitude.
14. Learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the 2nd Respondent
vehemently refuted the submissions of the Learned Counsel for the
Appellants. She argued that the Appellants were neither proper nor
necessary party to the petition before the Commission as no relief was
sought against them. She further argued that the Appellants cannot claim
to be parties aggrieved by the impugned order of the Commission as no
directions have been issued to them and the directions have been issued
only to the 3rd Respondent – GETCO. According to the Learned Senior
Counsel, except a bald assertion that the Appellants bear the transmission
charges of GETCO on residual basis, no material has been produced on
behalf of the Appellants to substantiate the said claim. It is also her
submission that the 2nd Respondent in its petition before the Commission,
had not sought exemption from payment of STOA charges and on the
contrary, prayer was for no discrimination amongst the consumers of private
as well as State Discoms in payment of STOA charges and by the
impugned order, the Commission has only directed GETCO to levy STOA
charges without any discrimination in terms of GERC Open Access
Regulations. She pointed out that the Commission found that the 2nd
Respondent did not utilise the state network for STOA and accordingly
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 8 of 19

directed GETCO to verify such claim and to refund STOA charges
recovered from 2nd Respondent which were party for procurement of inter-
state bilateral power exchange consumptions starting from 1st April, 2017
till the date of the impugned order. She argued that the claim of 2nd
Respondent for refund was with regards to the charges recovered by the
GETCO without utilization of GETCO network by the 2nd Respondent and
therefore, Appellants cannot establish any co-relation to refund of any such
charges by GETCO to 2nd Respondent.
15. Learned Senior Counsel further submitted that the Appellants had
knowledge, even prior to the passing of the impugned order by the
Commission, about the objection raised by GETCO with regards to the
discriminatory methodology employed by GETCO for levy of STOA charges
but the Appellants chose to remain silent and did not act thereby
acquiescing in passing of the tariff order dated 29th March, 2025 on the tariff
petition of GETCO as well as order dated 25th March, 2026 whereby ARR
of 2nd Respondent was approved for Financial Year 2026-27. She also cited
the judgement of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in H. Anjanappa and ors. Vs.
A. Prabhakar and ors. 2025 SCC online SC 183 to canvass that only that
person can prefer an appeal with the leave of the appellate court who is
adversely affected by the judgement and decree sought to be appealed
against and who was not a party to the original proceedings.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 9 of 19

16. We have considered the rival submissions of the Learned Counsels
and have perused impugned order of the Commission as well as the
relevant record.
17. Sub-Section (1) of the 111 of the Electricity Act, 2003 specifies who
can approach this Tribunal by way of appeal against an order of the
Commission and the same is extracted hereinbelow:-
“Section 111. (Appeal to Appellate Tribunal): ---
(1) Any person aggrieved by an order made by an adjudicating
officer under this Act (except under section 127) or an order made
by the Appropriate Commission under this Act may prefer an
appeal to the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity:
Provided that any person appealing against the order of the
adjudicating officer levying any penalty shall, while filing the
appeal , deposit the amount of such penalty:
Provided further that wherein any particular case, the Appellate
Tribunal is of the opinion that the deposit of such penalty would
cause undue hardship to such person, it may dispense with such
deposit subject to such conditions as it may deem fit to impose
so as to safeguard the realisation of penalty.”
18. The plain reading of this legal provision reveals that a person who is
aggrieved by the order of the Commission is competent to file appeal
against that order before this Tribunal. Therefore, a person who was a party
to the proceedings before the Commission and feels aggrieved by the order
passed by the Commission, has a statutory right to approach this Tribunal
by way of appeal under Section (1) of 111 of the Electricity Act, 2003.
However, in case a person, who was not a party to the proceedings before
the Commission but claims to be aggrieved by any order of the Commission
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 10 of 19

can assail the said order of the Commission before this Tribunal by way of
an appeal only after seeking leave of this Tribunal. What is important to bear
in mind is that any such person seeking leave of this Tribunal to file an
appeal against an order of the Commission, must satisfy this Tribunal,
before such leave is granted to him that he is in any manner aggrieved by
the said order. So, essentially, it is only that person who succeeds in
demonstrating that he has been affected by the order of the Commission,
who can seek leave of this Court to assail the said order. “Aggrieved” means
“Wronged”, “Harmed”, “Affected”, “Injured” etc. Thus, the person seeking
leave of this Tribunal to file an appeal against the Commission’s order must
demonstrate as to in what manner he is harmed or injured by that order.
19. The Hon’ble Supreme Court in H. Anjanappa judgement (supra) has
held that only where a judgement and decree prejudicially affected a person
who is not a party to the proceedings, that person can prefer an appeal with
the leave of that Appellate court. Further, upon referring to several previous
decisions of the apex court, following principles governing the grant of leave
to appeal have been succinctly evolved in the said judgement;
“i. Sections 96 and 100 of the CPC respectively provide for preferring
an appeal from an original decree or decree in appeal respectively;
ii. The said provisions do not enumerate the categories of persons who
can file an appeal;
iii. However, it a settled legal proposition that a stranger cannot be
permitted to file an appeal in any proceedings unless he satisfies the
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 11 of 19

court that he falls within the category of an aggrieved person;
iv. It is only where a judgment and decree prejudicially affects a person
who is not a party to the proceedings, he can prefer an appeal with the
leave of the court;
v. A person aggrieved, to file an appeal, must be one whose right is
affected by reason of the judgment and decree sought to be impugned;
vi. The expression “person aggrieved” does not include a person who
suffers from a psychological or an imaginary injury;
vii. It would be improper to grant leave to appeal to every person who
may in some remote or indirect way be prejudicially affected by a
decree or judgment; and
viii. Ordinarily leave to appeal should be granted to persons who,
though not parties to the proceedings, would be bound by the decree
or judgment in that proceeding and who would be precluded from
attacking its correctness in other proceedings.
20. Even though, the said judgement has been rendered by the Apex
Court in the context of Sections 96 & 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure,
1908, yet the above noted principles so evolved therein can profitably be
applied to the appeals under Section 111 of the Electricity Act, 2003 before
this Tribunal also for the reason that the power of the District Judge as well
as High Court hearing first appeals against the original decree of a Civil
Judge or a District Judge, as the case may be, are akin to the powers of
this Tribunal under Section 111 of the Act.
21. In the instant case, the impugned order dated 10th November, 2025
has been rendered by the Commission on a petition filed by 2nd Respondent
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 12 of 19

wherein the 2nd Respondent had prayed for refund of past period STOA
charges recovered from it by GETCO for the period from Financial Year
2017-18 and Financial Year 2024-25 with further direction to GETCO to
treat all Distribution Licensees including 2nd Respondent uniformally for
recovery of STOA charges for future period. The petition has been allowed
by the Commission and appropriate directions, as noted in paragraph No.
6 hereinabove, have been issued to GETCO. We were informed during the
hearing of the application that the GETCO has already filed a compliance
affidavit dated 8th January, 2026 to the effect that they would adhere to open
access mechanism for grant of STOA and levy of STOA charges without
any discrimination in line with the provisions of GERC Open Access
Regulations. It has further been stated in the affidavit that modality for
implementation of mechanism for grant of STOA and levy of STOA charges
are being worked out. Importantly, the GETCO also has stated in its affidavit
that claims submitted by 2nd Respondent have been verified and found to
be in order.
22. It is, thus, manifest that neither was any relief sought by the 2nd
Respondent in the petition before the Commission against the
Appellants/Applicants nor was any direction issued by the Commission to
the Appellants/Applicants in the impugned order. The issue before the
Commission was whether there had been any discrimination between the
State Discoms and private discoms with regards to the levy of STOA
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 13 of 19

charges, as contended by the 2nd Respondent in its petition, which has been
answered by the Commission in the impugned order. The directions to
GETCO to refund the past period STOA charges recovered by it from 2nd
Respondent was only a consequential one. In these circumstances, we are
unable to comprehend as to how the Appellants claim to be affected or
aggrieved by the impugned order of the Commission.
23. Learned Counsel for the Appellants/Applicants argued that since they
are paying the state transmission charges on residual basis, they are an
“affected party” as the reduction in charges for STOA qua the 2nd
Respondent would increase the financial burden upon the Appellants. We
do not see any force in this argument. The fallacy of this argument is evident
from the fact that the Commission has directed the refund of STOA charges
recovered by GETCO from the 2nd Respondent while observing that the 2nd
Respondent was not utilising the state network which is indicated in the
paragraph No. 26 of the impugned order:-
“26. As regards refund of STOA Charges paid by TPI, for past
period, we have noted that TPL has direct connectivity
with ISTS Network. TPL has also claimed that it does not
utilise State Network for short term Open Access and
stated that the same can be verified by GETCO from the
data available with GETCO. GETCO is the owner of
Transmission Network and has details of imports/exports
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 14 of 19

at various interconnection points with ISTS as well as
TPL. In our view, the aspect of intelligible differentia also
supports the prayer of the Petitioner for refund of STOA
charges, particularly when the Petitioner has not been
utilizing the Intra-state Network of GETCO for sourcing of
power through STOA in addition to the ground to give
uniform treatment to the consumers of State DISCOMs
and TPL. Accordingly, we direct GETCO to verify the
claim of TPL within 2 months from the date of this order.
Upon verification of STOA charges recovered from TPL,
GETCO should refund such STOA Charges paid for
procurement of inter-state bilateral and Power Exchange
Transactions starting from 01.04.2017 till the date of this
Order for Inter-State Short Term Bilateral and Power
Exchange Open Access Transmissions in six equal
monthly instalments.”
24. Manifestly, the Commission did not grant blanket exemption to the 2nd
Respondent and had directed the 3rd Respondent GETCO to verify such
claim of 2nd Respondent. As already noted hereinabove, the 3rd Respondent
– GETCO had verified the claim of 2nd Respondent for refund of STOA
charges in terms of the impugned order of the Commission and has found
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 15 of 19

the same to be in order. Under these circumstances also, it is difficult to say
that the Appellants are “affected” or “aggrieved” by the impugned order .
25. It is true that the 3rd Respondent – GETCO had objected to the
maintainability of the petition before the Commission on account of non-
impleadment of State Distribution Licensees i.e. the Appellants. In our
opinion, the objection has been rightly over-ruled by the Commission in the
impugned order upon observing that the 2nd Respondent has not sought
any relief against the State Discoms and that the STOA charges recovered
by SLDC are approved by the Commission in the tariff order in relation to
GETCO. Be that as it may, the fact remains that the Appellants appear to
have been aware about the proceedings of the petition before the
Commission but instead of initiating steps for being impleaded in those
proceedings, chose to maintain silence. Therefore, having chosen to avoid
seeking implementation before the Commission, the Appellants cannot be
heard to raise their non-impleadment as a ground for seeking leave to
appeal.
26. Even if, for the sake of arguments, it is assumed that the Appellants
are “aggrieved parties” with regards to the impugned order of the
Commission, it is to be noted that they had three opportunities to participate
in the proceedings before the Commission on the aspect on which they are
seeking to assail the impugned order in this appeal. First such occasion
was on 24th February, 2025 when public hearing was conducted by the
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 16 of 19

Commission in the tariff petition filed by GETCO i.e. case No. 2419 of 2024.
2nd such occasion was when the Commission passed order dated 29th
March, 2025 in the said tariff petition of GETCO suggesting the 2nd
Respondent to file a separate petition with regards to its objection to the
discriminatory levy of STOA charges. 3rd such occasion was when the 2nd
Respondent filed petition No. 2491 of 2025 in which the impugned order
has been passed. 4th such occasion was subsequent to the passing of the
impugned order when the order dated 25th March, 2026 was passed by the
Commission on the petition of 2nd Respondent for Financial Year 2026-27,
duly factoring the refund as per the impugned order. Pertinently, the said
order dated 25th March, 2026 has not been challenged by the Appellants. It
is not the case of the Appellants that they were oblivious about all these
proceedings or did not have any occasion to get knowledge about these
proceedings. Undisputedly, public notices were issued in all these petitions
and public hearings were held, as is a mandatory requirement.
27. The Appellants appear to have consciously decided not to participate
any of these proceedings concerning the discriminatory levy of STOA
charges, as contended by the 2nd Respondent, which indicates that they
were not vigilant in exercising their legal rights and, therefore, are precluded
from seeking leave of this Court to assail the impugned order of the
Commission now when it has already been implemented.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 17 of 19

28. With regards to the contentions on behalf of the Appellants that they
were signatories to the TSA dated 1st April, 2005 and, therefore, ought to
have been impleaded as parties before the Commission, it would be suffice
to note that the Commission has not passed any operative order with
regards to the TSA and, therefore, non-impleadment of the Appellants does
not affect the legality of the impugned order.
29. Reliance on behalf of the Appellants on the Emmar MGF case (supra)
and Municipal Corporation of Bombay case (supra) is totally misplaced. In
the Emmar case, the Appellant Emmar MGF Construction Pvt. Ltd. was an
aggrieved person as it had to comply with the impugned order. At the same
time, this Tribunal in that case held the Government of NCT of Delhi not to
be a necessary party to the appeal as the interest of the Government was
not adversely affected by the order appealed therein. Thus, in a way, this
judgement supports the case of the 2nd Respondent and does not advance
the case of the Appellants. In so far as the Municipal Corporation judgement
of the Hon’ble Supreme Court is concerned, the apex court noted that the
exercise of power by the Municipal Corporation would affect the interest of
a class or classes of persons as the proceedings are not inter se, “parties
ranged on opposite sides”, which is not the case herein.
30. In the light of the above discussion, we are of the considered opinion
that the Appellants do not fall in the category of “aggrieved person” as
neither has any direction been issued against them in the impugned order
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA No. 274 of 2026 in DFR No. 70 of 2026 Page 18 of 19

nor are they in any manner affected by the impugned order of the
Commission. As held by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in H. Anjanappa
judgement, it would not be appropriate to grant leave to appeal to every
person who may in some remote or indirect way be prejudicially affected by
the orders sought to be appealed against. The Appellants would, at best,
fall into such category and, therefore, are not entitled to leave to appeal.
31. Resultantly, we do not find any merit in the instant application. The
same is hereby dismissed. However, we make it clear that our observations
in this order are confined to the instant application alone whereby
Appellants had sought leave to appeal and no such observations shall be
construed as our opinion on the merits of the case.
DFR No. 70 of 2026
32. In view of the dismissal of the IA No. 274 of 2026, whereby the
Appellants had sought leave to appeal, the instant appeal also stands
dismissed as not maintainable.
Pronounced in the open court on this 28th day of September , 2026.
Virender Bhat Seema Gupta
Judicial Member Officiating Chairperson
